# Market Intelligence: Tenant Feature Guide
**generated by `4.250111.x` for `4.25111.66` on Sept 8, 2026.**  
**generated by `4.250111.x` from `4.25111.131` on Sept 29, 2026.**  


What a tenant can do with this product, and the click-path to do it. Each
feature names the guarantee the platform makes behind it (from the capability
map), then a concrete workflow a tenant user performs in the web UI.

Administrative features are collapsed to a single entry at the end, as
requested.

---

## 1. Register a workspace and sign in

**What it is.** A tenant creates an isolated workspace. From that point every
piece of their data (topics, posts, keys, spend) is fenced off from every other
tenant at the database level, and nothing is reachable without a valid identity.
A workspace is only ever created for an email address its owner has verified.

**Guarantee behind it.** No identity, no tenant, no data, you get a 403 (C1).
A tenant can never observe or mutate another tenant's rows (A2), and a
cross-tenant reference is impossible to even represent (A3).

**Workflow (start from a plan).**
1. On the marketing site, open Pricing, choose a plan, and select Purchase.
2. Create your login (or sign in) when asked, then complete checkout with the
   payment provider.
3. On Set Up Your Workspace, enter the Organization Name, then choose how the
   workspace pays for AI: Start on the platform trial key included with my
   purchase, or Use my own API key (choose the AI Vendor, Select Model, enter
   the LLM API Key, and Verify Key).
4. Select Create Workspace. You are the owner, and you land on the dashboard
   (the Command Center).

**Workflow (set up first, then choose a plan).**
1. On the marketing site, open Get Started and select Create Your Account.
2. Follow the verification link in the email you receive. Verification is
   required.
3. Sign in and select Set Up My Workspace: name the workspace and connect your
   AI model key.
4. Choose a plan on the billing page. The subscription activates at checkout.

**Invited by your organization?** Use the link in your invitation email; it
carries your workspace assignment. If you sign in and see "No Membership", log
out and back in after verifying your email, and the invitation is accepted
automatically.

Everything you do from here is scoped to your workspace automatically.

---

## 2. Define what the workspace writes about (Topics and Content Angles)

**What it is.** The tenant tells the pipeline its subject matter: topics to
cover, and for each topic the content angles that frame posts, the hashtags,
the domain tags that match sources, and a weight that sets how often the topic
comes up. This is the steering wheel for all automated content. The writing
style (genre) is chosen per post when composing, not on the topic.

**Guarantee behind it.** Configuration is data, validated at the database, not
in loose application code (D5), so a malformed topic is rejected rather than
silently mishandled.

**Workflow.**
1. Dashboard, open Topics (Topic Management).
2. Select + Add Topic and fill in Topic Name, Description (one sentence),
   Scope, Content Angles, Hashtags, Domain Tags, and Weight.
3. Optionally select Generate Suggestions to have AI propose angles and
   hashtags for the topic.
4. Select Save Topic. When feeds are discovered for the topic, review them and
   select Add Selected Feeds.
5. On a saved topic, Details opens its Research Instructions, where search
   instructions can be tuned per angle. The research pipeline uses all of this
   on its next cycle.

---

## 3. Generate a post with AI

**What it is.** The core act. The tenant triggers the research-and-generate
pipeline: feeds and web search are gathered, corroborated into a verified
brief, and an LLM drafts a business social post from a vaulted prompt. The run
uses the workspace's own AI key, or the platform trial key when the workspace
was purchased without one. Only models the platform operator has enabled can
run; any other is refused before a call is made.

**Guarantee behind it.** A post is never generated from thin sources (D1).
Numbers in the post are never invented; only figures present in the research are
used (D3). Every untrusted input, including the model's own output, passes the
same safety gate (D2). The prompt text itself lives in memory for one call and
is never logged or returned (B4).

**Workflow.**
1. Dashboard, Quick Actions: select Generate for a one-step post on a topic,
   or select Create and choose a Topic, an Angle, and a Genre, then Generate
   with AI. (With no genre chosen, Create starts a blank New Post you write
   yourself.)
2. The pipeline researches, then drafts. Watch progress in Research Monitor.
3. The generated post lands in Awaiting Approval with the status Pending
   Approval, with its Sources Referenced and Quality Breakdown attached. (It is
   saved as a draft first, so a lost connection never loses the paid content,
   then promoted as soon as the full reply is stored.) A blank New Post stays a
   draft until you write it.

---

## 4. Review sources and the quality assessment

**What it is.** Before trusting a post, the tenant inspects what it was built
from and how it scored, so publishing is an informed choice rather than a leap.

**Guarantee behind it.** The verified-brief step means claims are corroborated
across independent sources before they reach the draft (D1, D3). The tenant sees
exactly that provenance.

**Workflow.**
1. In Awaiting Approval, open the post.
2. Read the Sources Referenced list (the feeds and web results behind it).
3. Read the Quality Breakdown: an overall score and the individual scores
   (such as hook, authenticity, source grounding, and factual caution).
4. Decide: edit, approve, schedule, or discard.

---

## 5. Edit a post before it goes out

**What it is.** The tenant refines wording, title, or attached media on a post
that has not been published.

**Guarantee behind it.** Editing keeps the post in its pre-publication state;
nothing about an edit publishes anything (D4). The safety gate still applies to
the edited text on the way out (D2).

**Workflow.**
1. Open a post awaiting approval (or a draft) and choose Edit Post.
2. Adjust Title and Content.
3. Attach or Detach an image if desired. Attaching an AI generated image needs
   the Image Studio capability (Individual Plus or Business Plus).
4. Save. The post keeps its place, now updated.

---

## 6. Approve and publish (the human gate)

**What it is.** The deliberate act that sends a post to LinkedIn. In manual mode
the tenant approves; nothing reaches LinkedIn without this.

**Guarantee behind it.** Nothing publishes without a human act (D4). Publish
intent is exactly-once, degrading to at-most-once, never duplicated (E1). If an
attached image can't be read, the post fails loudly rather than posting broken
(E3).

**Workflow.**
1. In Awaiting Approval, open a post with the status Pending Approval.
2. Review the final PREVIEW.
3. Approve to publish now, or Schedule it for a chosen time. The platform
   publishes to the connected LinkedIn identity.
4. The post moves to a Published state with its LinkedIn reference recorded. A
   too-long post is returned to Pending Approval, editable, rather than marked
   failed.

---

## 7. Choose automatic vs manual generation (Mode)

**What it is.** The tenant decides whether queued posts publish automatically,
or wait for manual approval every time.

**Guarantee behind it.** Even in automatic mode the same output filter and
exactly-once publish intent apply (D2, E1); mode changes convenience, not the
correctness guarantees.

**Workflow.**
1. Dashboard, open the Automation card.
2. Select Manual (approve each) or Auto.
3. In Auto, generation runs on the scheduler's cadence, and a queued post
   publishes only after it has waited the workspace's review window, so there
   is always time to intervene. In Manual, posts wait in Awaiting Approval.

---

## 8. Connect a LinkedIn destination

**What it is.** The tenant links the LinkedIn identity that posts will publish
to, either a personal profile or an organization page.

**Guarantee behind it.** An organization page can only be attached if the live
LinkedIn ACL actually grants it (E4), and the destination is stamped once and
never silently changed (E2). Credentials are encrypted per tenant, never stored
in plaintext (B1, B2).

**Workflow.**
1. Dashboard, open LinkedIn Connection. Status shows the current connection.
2. Under App Credentials, enter the Client id and Client secret, then select
   Store App Credentials.
3. Select Reconnect LinkedIn to authorize and obtain tokens. (Set Tokens
   Manually accepts an Access Token and Refresh Token directly, with Store
   Token Pair.)
4. Under Publish as, choose Personal profile or Organization Page. For an
   organization, select Connect Org Page (run discovery); only pages LinkedIn
   grants you are offered.
5. The workspace can now publish to that identity.

---

## 9. Generate an AI image for a post (Image Studio)

**What it is.** The tenant creates an AI image to accompany a post, with cost
controlled up front. Image Studio is included in the Individual Plus and
Business Plus plans.

**Guarantee behind it.** No image renders without an exact pre-spend estimate
and a cleared budget gate, checked before the vendor is ever called (F2). Every
charge lands in an append-only ledger that is the sole authority (F3).

**Workflow.**
1. First, in User Management, set the Image Render Budget (USD per cycle) and
   the Image Generation Provider. Without a budget the studio refuses to
   generate.
2. Open Image Studio and describe the image you want. Choose a Story Lens (the
   image style, such as an editorial photo).
3. The studio shows the spend estimate and checks it against the budget. If
   the budget clears, the image renders; if the cycle's budget is used up, you
   are stopped before any charge.
4. Optionally Refine the image.
5. Attach the resulting image to a post.

---

## 10. Track performance (Analytics)

**What it is.** The tenant sees how published content is doing: posts, topic
performance, the best times to post, follower demographics, and an AI written
narrative summary.

**Guarantee behind it.** Statelessness is real and every cache is derivable
(G2), so the numbers shown are reproducible from source data rather than a
drifting side store.

**Workflow.**
1. Dashboard, open Analytics and choose a Window (the time range).
2. Select Sync Now to pull the latest LinkedIn figures, or Reload to refresh.
3. Review Posts, Performance by Topic, Posting Time Heatmap, and Follower
   Demographics. Select Narrative summary for a written overview.
4. Workspaces with employee advocacy also see Advocacy Program Intelligence
   and Advocacy Amplification.
5. For the cycle-by-cycle history of what the agent did, use the Activity Log
   on the dashboard.

---

## 11. Employee advocacy (Organization Manager)

**What it is.** A tenant with an organization amplifies a source post through its
members: each enabled member gets a personalized variant they can publish from
their own profile. Employee advocacy is included in the Business Plus plan.

**Guarantee behind it.** A member secret exposes exactly one member, never the
whole tenant (B3). Member credentials are isolated per member, and the tenant
boundary still holds around the whole feature (A2, B2).

**Workflow.**
1. Open Advocacy.
2. In Members, select Enable Member for each employee who opts in. Optionally
   Add Voice Note to capture a member's tone, style, and audience.
3. Under Generate Variants, pick a Source post and select Generate Variant
   Post.
4. Each member reviews their variant in the Post Variants Queue under My
   Participation, and sets their Publishing mode: Manual: I approve every
   post, or Auto: publish approved variants for me.
5. A member's variant publishes from their own profile, in their chosen mode.

---

## 12. Manage the plan and vendor key (Billing and Entitlement)

**What it is.** The tenant selects a plan, which unlocks capabilities, and
supplies its own AI vendor key. Billing is about entitlement, not the platform
handling card money.

| Plan | Adds |
|---|---|
| Individual | the core product |
| Individual Plus | Image Studio |
| Business | Organization Manager |
| Business Plus | Organization Manager, Employee Advocacy, and Image Studio |

Individual and Business start with a 5-day grace period before the first
30-day cycle.

**Guarantee behind it.** A capability requires both entitlement and an operator
flag, denied by default (C5). Suspension halts writes but never locks the tenant
out of billing, so they can always fix a lapse (C6). The platform never sees a
card (F5), and no secret ever appears in the spend ledger (B5).

**Workflow.**
1. Dashboard, open Billing (Plans And Pricing) and Choose A Plan.
2. Complete Purchase through the payment provider (the platform records
   entitlement, not the card). To change or cancel later, use the payment
   provider's customer portal, linked from Billing.
3. In User Management, under AI Language Provider, choose the Provider and
   Model, enter your API Key, and select Verify Key, so generation runs on your
   own account. A workspace purchased on the platform trial key runs on that
   key until you add your own.
4. Capabilities unlock according to the plan.
5. Watch AI spend in User Management, under Spend: Recent Activity lists each
   workflow's calls, tokens, rates, model, and key source; Aggregate Totals
   summarize by provider and key source.
